text: Which is the best reason to write a loop rather than a stream pipeline?
choices: The computation is not map, filter or reduce — some stage would resist being named.
The team is unfamiliar with streams, so the loop will be correct more often.
The result must be mutable, which a pipeline cannot produce.
The collection has fewer than a thousand elements, below which streams do not pay off.
explanation: Name what each stage does; if one resists, the decomposition failed and the loop was right. The other honest cases are needing an index, iterating two collections in step (Java has no `zip`), an early exit conditioned on accumulated state, and mutation. Team fluency is a real consideration but an argument for consistency, and `collect(toList())` yields a mutable list.
